title.narrative: Investing in Social Protection for Inclusion, Resilience, and Efficiency (INSPIRE) Project

description.narrative: The Additional Financing (AF) will bridge the reforms supported by the original INSPIRE project and other World Bank-financed operations with the next generation of Social Safety Net (SSN) reforms. It leverages the World Bank engagement in social protection sector in Ukraine, helping to sustain the provision of social benefits to over 2.6 million people during the war, enhancing existing systems and programs, and contributing to longer-term post-war recovery efforts. Twenty-nine types of benefits financed by the project provide social relief to low-income and energy-vulnerable households, vulnerable families, children, and students, as well as persons with disabilities. The AF will support structural improvements of the social assistance system to be achieved through (i) piloting a new Basic Income Benefit (BIB) program, which represents a major shift in social policy by combining various benefits into a single, efficient, shock-responsive, and inclusive program; (ii) further expanding the Guaranteed Minimum Income – Ukraine's main anti-poverty social assistance program - to support low-income families during the transition to the BIB; (iii) improving the administration of benefits; (iv) introducing rent subsidies and people-centric social services to strengthen support for Internally Displaced Persons; (v) and enhancing access to affordable childcare for vulnerable families. This comprehensive and cohesive reform package will help accelerate and scale up the modernization of the SSNs, paving the way for introducing the BIB program to significantly enhance support for vulnerable groups.

The development objective is to (i) contribute to sustaining the government's capacity to provide social support to the poor and vulnerable during the war: (ii) support the government's scale-up capacity to expand social support to the vulnerable during the war and beyond, and (iii) build a foundation for sustainable recovery by improving access to and quality of social and employment services for the poor and IDPs.

title.narrative: The Borrower has completed verification of IDP assistance beneficiariesâ€™ data using the UISSS to verify their compliance with the improved eligibility criteria for this type of social assistance

comment.narrative: During August 2023, the information about beneficiaries of the social assistance for internally displaced persons to cover living expenses was verified, and this included the following phases: 1. The Ministry of Social Policy has transferred to the Ministry of Finance of Ukraine (MoF) information from the Unified Information System of the Social Sphere (UISSS) regarding 2.7 million recipients of the social assistance for internally displaced persons to cover living expenses as on August 1, 2023 for the purpose of its verification in accordance with the Law of Ukraine "On Verification and Monitoring of State Benefits". 2. To verify compliance with the improved procedure, the MoF has carried out two waves of data verification procedures using the appropriate registers. Based on the results of the completed verification, the MoF has submitted 181 309 recommendations to the Ministry of Social Policy regarding the discrepancies found, which were uploaded into the UISSS for their further processing. In accordance with the Verification Protocols for PBCs, the PBC is considered to be achieved if, as on October 1, 2023, at least 50% of the recommendations provided by the MoF based on the results of the verification have been implemented by the structural units for social protection of the population. As on October 01, 2023, the structural subdivisions for social protection of the population have processed 129 827 recommendations, i.e. 71.61% of the total number of recommendations provided by the MoF as a result of the verification. The main factor that led to the ceases of the social assistance for internally displaced persons to cover living expenses is the staying the person abroad for more than 30 calendar days in a row (58.1% of cease cases for IDP benefit to cover living expenses). The next most significant factor that led to the ceases of the benefit payment is the presence of residential premises/parts of a residential premises located in the territory not included in the list of occupied territories or territories of active hostilities or included in the list of territories where date of the end of active hostilities (possibility of active hostilities) or temporary occupation is known (16.6% of cease cases for IDP benefit to cover living expenses). The third most significant factor that led to the ceases of payment is the presence of moneys in the IDP's deposit bank account (accounts) or bonds of the internal state loan in the total amount exceeding UAH 100,000. (15.2% of cease cases for IDP benefit to cover living expenses).
